arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Cohen argued the Act only applies when stopping state revenue.
Mr. Hungar argued the Act bars suits restraining state tax assessments.
Mr. Goddard argued the Act has a very broad reach.
Chief Justice Rehnquist noted the case is submitted.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of the Tax Injunction Act. The statute limits federal court power over state taxes. The parties dispute whether a tax credit counts as a tax.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines the boundary between federal and state judicial power. It determines whether citizens can challenge state tax credits in federal court. The outcome shapes the balance of comity between the two systems.
